en.name: NexusTransferPay
en.short_description: Currency converter with live ECB reference rates and rate history
en.description:
NexusTransferPay is a currency converter and exchange-rate tracker from American Group LLC, for anyone who sends money abroad and wants to know what a fair rate looks like first. Every rate in the app is a reference rate published by the European Central Bank and delivered by the free Frankfurter service, and the app shows the date each rate applies to.

CONVERT
Type an amount, pick the currency you have and the currency you want, and see the converted amount at the latest reference rate, with the rate shown both ways. Swap the pair with one tap; the app remembers the last pair you used. It covers the 30 or so currencies the European Central Bank publishes, including the US dollar, euro, British pound, Indian rupee, Mexican peso, Brazilian real, Philippine peso, Japanese yen and the Canadian and Australian dollars.

RATE HISTORY
A chart of the pair's daily reference rate over one month, three months or a year, with the low, the high and the change over the period.

RATES
Every published rate against a base currency you choose, each with its inverse. Tap a currency to see its history.

CHECK A TRANSFER QUOTE
When a bank or transfer service gives you a quote, enter what it says the recipient will get and the fee it charges. NexusTransferPay works out the effective rate you are being offered and what the quote costs compared with the reference rate, as an amount and as a percentage: the margin that is usually hidden in the exchange rate.

NO INVENTED NUMBERS
When the rate feed cannot be reached, the app says the rates are unavailable and shows no converted amount. It never presents a stale or made-up rate as the current one.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
NexusTransferPay does not send or receive money, hold balances or connect to a bank account. Reference rates are not quotes: banks and transfer services add a margin, and the European Central Bank publishes once per working day, so rates do not change during the day or at weekends. The app gives no financial advice. There are no accounts, no sign-in and no in-app purchases. It needs a network connection to load rates.

ADS
NexusTransferPay is free and shows ads from Google AdMob: a banner on the converter and rates screens, and occasionally a full-screen ad when you switch between them. Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure ads. The app does not track you across other companies' apps, and where the law requires it (the EEA, the UK and Switzerland) you are asked for consent before any ad is requested; you can change that choice later under Privacy choices in Settings.

The interface is in 25 languages. Currency names come from the rate feed in English.

American Group LLC - www.americangroup.ai
Support: contact@americangroup.ai

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
NexusTransferPay is a currency converter and exchange-rate tracker from American Group LLC, for anyone who sends money abroad and wants to know what a fair rate looks like first. Every rate in the app is a reference rate published by the European Central Bank and delivered by the free Frankfurter service, and the app shows the date each rate applies to.

Intended audience:
General consumer audience; no specialist knowledge is assumed.

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. Every feature is reachable from the first screen after launch.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Frankfurter (api.frankfurter.dev) — European Central Bank reference exchange rates
- Firebase Crashlytics, Analytics and Performance Monitoring — crash reports and usage diagnostics, not linked to a person
- Google AdMob (ads) — banner and interstitial ads; Google may use device identifiers to serve and measure ads; consent-based via Google's User Messaging Platform, no App Tracking Transparency prompt and no tracking

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app follows the device language for 25 locales (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, bn, fa, fil, id, nl, pl, sv, ta, te, th, tr, ur, vi), but translation is partial: shared labels are translated, while most screen text is in English only. Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

_was_blocked_resolved.note: Failure paths, sign-out and the fabricated credit factors were fixed on 2026-09-15. Copy and the finance-category licensing/disclosure text must still come from the product owner, and nobody has confirmed the backend is reachable.

previous.no_copy_drafted: Copy deliberately not drafted — regulated category, unverified backend.
previous.evidence: Screens cover transfers, cards, loans, insurance, credit score and an AI chat (lib/screens/*). All of it runs against kBaseUrl = https://nexustransferpay.app (core/api_service.dart), which this sandbox cannot reach, so I cannot confirm a single transfer, loan or credit-score feature actually functions against a live backend. What has been confirmed is the failure behaviour: as of 2026-09-15 a transfer that does not come back with a receipt is reported as a failure and never as a success, and a release build shows a Service unavailable state rather than sample figures (test/transfer_failure_test.dart, 21 tests). Sign out now clears the stored session and leaves the signed-in shell, and the credit-score factor bars are drawn only from figures the bureau returned. Writing 'send money to anyone' for a money-transmission app whose backend I could not reach is still a claim I am not willing to make, and both stores apply extra scrutiny to the finance category.
previous.to_unblock: Copy must come from the product owner, together with the licensing and disclosure text both stores require for a financial-services listing.
